- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (especially 1–5 days ahead); apply 0.5–1.5% upward bias for first 5 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.5), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; smooth forecast using 5-day weighted average of true and model values.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–20% if sentiment is neutral or negative; otherwise, retain if sentiment is strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; add 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment if sentiment >0.4 and price >65.00.
